label: Fires at D2 when a1 led rarely to S2, growing in the episode's second half.
explanation: Silent at D1 and GO. At D2 it is driven almost entirely by the observed rare transition a1 -> S2 (in_action == 1, in_state == 2). Its size grows with episode time: near zero early, then a steep linear ramp after about trial 60, reaching ~2 near trial 99. The (ep_trial >= 30) step gets a negative weight and only corrects the timing baseline for these steps. Other D2 transitions (a1 S1, a2 S2, a2 S1) stay at zero, so the timing baseline overpredicts them. Previous-trial reward/choice, belief_lo and belief_cover add only ~0.01 in the free fit; the free fit mostly refines the shape of the episode-time ramp with step functions. The remaining variance is that some late a1->S2 trials do not fire at all, which no observed history term captured.

issues: The core claim holds. The feature is zero at D1 and GO and is driven only by the rare a1 -> S2 transition at D2. In the profile, the D2 residual by choice x state is +0.159 for code 5 (a1 S2) and about -0.02 for every other code.

The timing in the label is wrong. 'Growing in the episode's second half' suggests onset near trial 50, but the step (in_state==2)*(in_action==1)*(ep_trial>=60) scores only 0.347 on test. A ramp from 50 scores 0.552, from 60 scores 0.610, from 70 scores 0.658, from 75 scores 0.664 and from 80 scores 0.645. The feature really switches on around trial 70-75, in the last quarter of the episode.
The second short-form term is a fitted correction, not a description. Adding (ep_trial >= 30) with a negative weight moves test R^2 only from 0.610 to 0.615.

The magnitude is mostly on/off, not graded. In misses, the late a1->S2 steps sit at about 1.4-2.0 or at exactly 0 (for example t87, t91 and t97 are 0 while their neighbours are 1.5-2.0). The single linear ramp predicts about 1.0 for all of them, so the 'ramp' mostly reflects a rising chance of firing. Which late a1->S2 trials fire is unexplained; this is the main remaining error.

Observed terms add little and none explains the on/off pattern. A belief_lo term gives +0.016 (free fit, test 0.680), prev_action==1 +0.011, belief_cover, prev_reward, prev_common and the trial-2 reward about +0.00. The D2 belief-decile trend in the profile goes away once the a1->S2 x ramp term is in, because it only reflects how often a1 is chosen.
There are no large systematic errors by phase or previous trial with the ramp-75 short form. The largest is about -0.03 at D2, which is the timing baseline overpredicting the other transitions.
skeptic.revised_label: Fires at D2 after a rare a1 -> S2 transition, increasingly from about trial 75 on.
